# Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore)

## Basic profile and purpose

Alexandra Hospital (AH) is a 326-bed **integrated general hospital** located at 378 Alexandra Road in Queenstown, Singapore. Since 1 June 2018 it has been managed by the **National University Health System (NUHS)** and serves about **100 000 residents** in the Queenstown precinct and the wider southwest region. As the first integrated general hospital in Singapore, AH provides **holistic care across acute, sub-acute and rehabilitative settings** so that patients do not need to transfer to another institution. Its clinical model is team-led and programme-based: patients are placed under at least one of five core programmes ("Be Better", "Get Better", "Live Better", "Age Better" and "Cope Better") and are looked after by a single principal doctor and the same care team.

The hospital's purpose statement is **"We redesign healthcare with and for humanity"**, reflecting AH's ambition to transform care models through innovation and partnership with the community. This purpose aligns with NUHS's wider vision and mission to advance healthcare through education and research while delivering incredible care.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Basic profile and purpose

### Location and facilities

AH occupies a **historic colonial-style campus** built in the late 1930s on 110 000 m2 of land. Located adjacent to the Rail Corridor and Queenstown MRT, the campus includes original British military hospital blocks (some gazetted for conservation) and modern wings. Gardens surrounding the hospital contain over **500 plant species** and **100 butterfly species**, including a **20-hectare medicinal garden** opened in July 2005 that was based on a book by botanist Wee Yeow Chin. A **Therapeutic Horticulture Programme** was launched in November 2019 to provide occupational therapy to patients through gardening.

text: ## Historical overview

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Historical overview

text:
### Early years and wartime history

* **1938-1940:** The British Military Hospital (later Alexandra Hospital) was built and opened as a 356-bed facility to serve the British Far East Command. Before the hospital was built, the site housed a malaria ward around 1910.
* **World War II:** During the Japanese invasion of Singapore, the hospital became the site of a massacre. In February 1942 Japanese soldiers killed around **200 patients and staff**, despite the building being marked with Red Cross symbols. The hospital expanded to 550 beds and treated up to 900 patients during the war.
* **Post-war:** After the liberation of Singapore, the hospital returned to British control until September 1971 when it was handed over to the Singapore Ministry of Health for **S$1** and renamed **Alexandra Road General Hospital**.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Historical overview > Early years and wartime history

text:
### Singapore administration and modern milestones

* **1975:** AH performed Southeast Asia's first successful limb re-attachment surgery and opened Singapore's first self-dependency dialysis centre in partnership with the National Kidney Foundation.
* **1994-1995:** The first geriatric centre in Singapore was established at AH. In 1995 the National University of Singapore's medical school adopted the hospital as part of its campus.
* **1998:** The hospital was declared a historic site by the National Heritage Board.
* **2008:** Alexandra Health System cluster was formed, including AH and the new Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.
* **2015-2018:** JurongHealth used the site as a holding facility for Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, followed by Sengkang Health until 2018. On **1 June 2018** NUHS took over the hospital and pioneered the Integrated General Hospital (IGH) model.
* **Archaeological finds:** Excavations in 2021 uncovered charred Japanese wartime literature, water bottles and helmets buried at the campus. These artefacts, likely hidden during Japan's surrender, will be exhibited in the redeveloped hospital's heritage gallery.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Historical overview > Singapore administration and modern milestones

## Future Alexandra Campus

AH is undergoing a **major redevelopment** into a larger integrated campus that will open progressively from **2028**. Key features include:

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Future Alexandra Campus

text:
*major redevelopment** into a larger integrated campus that will open progressively from **2028**. Key features include:

* **Increased capacity:** The redeveloped campus will have about **1 300 beds**, up from the current 326, to meet future healthcare demand. A March 2025 Ministry of Health press release confirms that the campus will open from **2028**.
* **Integrated care model:** The campus will be Singapore's first hospital providing a **seamless continuum of care from acute to rehabilitative settings**, reducing the need for transfers. It will continue to emphasise general medicine, geriatrics, palliative care, rehabilitation, psychiatry and generalist surgery.
* **Six peaks of excellence:** Integrated care, geriatric medicine, supportive and palliative care, rehabilitative medicine, psychological medicine and ambulatory surgery. Psychiatric services, including child and adolescent psychiatry and psychogeriatrics, will be expanded.
* **Pandemic- and future-proof design:** The new campus will be zero-carbon, energy-efficient and "phygital" (integrating physical and digital care). Designs include mass screening areas, negative-pressure zones, a command centre and modular wards to handle outbreaks.
* **Two high-rise buildings and expanded land:** The project will enlarge the land area from 12.2 ha to **13.3 ha** and add two high-rise buildings. Construction will start in 2025 and take about ten years.
* **Integrated community spaces:** The campus will be linked with the Rail Corridor and the upcoming Queenstown Health District, featuring green spaces, memory markers and a heritage trail.
* **Expansion of emergency services:** While AH currently operates a 24-hour Urgent Care Centre, emergency ambulances have not conveyed patients since 2015. From **1 October 2025** ambulances with non-life-threatening conditions are being routed to AH's Urgent Care Centre during weekday daytime hours. The redeveloped hospital will eventually host a full emergency department.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Future Alexandra Campus

text:
## Integrated General Hospital (IGH) model

AH pioneered Singapore's **Integrated General Hospital** model. The core principle is **"One patient, One bed, One care team, One principal doctor, One with the community and Healthcare redesign (OOOOOH)"**. Patients receive care from a multidisciplinary firm led by a generalist who coordinates all specialty consultations. Over 90 % of patients discharged from 2019-2025 saw only one principal doctor. The model reduces fragmentation by consolidating multiple medical conditions under one physician and ensures smooth transitions from hospital to home.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Integrated General Hospital (IGH) model

text:
### Core programmes

AH organizes care through several clinical programmes, each aligned with the IGH philosophy:

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Integrated General Hospital (IGH) model > Core programmes

text:
- **Integrated Medicine Programme** | The largest programme, covering 12 specialties including advanced internal medicine, cardiology, dermatology, endocrinology, gastroenterology & hepatology, haematology, infectious diseases, neurology, psychological medicine, renal medicine, respiratory medicine and rheumatology. Care is delivered through generalist-led wards and the **I-Care Clinic**, with a single principal doctor coordinating specialty input. Features include a **Virtual Care Centre**, transitional care programme and telemonitoring services.
- **Well Programme** | Focuses on preventive care to help individuals "Be Better". Clinics include the **Exercise Clinic**, which provides exercise prescriptions for chronic diseases; the **Healthy Longevity Research Clinic**, offering personalised preventive care using biomarkers and geroscience principles; the **Integrated Women's Clinic** for women approaching menopause; an **Occupational Medicine Clinic** focusing on workplace health; and a **Staff Clinic** for employees. The programme aims to provide one-stop care by consolidating appointments and health checks.
- **Healthy Ageing Programme** | Aims to maximise physical, mental and social well-being of seniors. Services include a dedicated **Geriatric Ward** ("Rasa Sayang") and the **EMERALD Unit** for patients with delirium or dementia, which uses a restraint-free environment, orientation cues and inter-generational therapy. Outpatient services comprise general geriatric, memory, falls and balance, Parkinson disease, continence and other clinics. Community geriatrics programmes (EMBRACE) and nurse-led home care (NIC) support patients after discharge.
- **Supportive & Palliative Care Programme** | Provides holistic, multidisciplinary care for patients with life-limiting illnesses such as advanced cancer, organ failure, advanced dementia or Parkinson's disease. Services span inpatient (Ward 5 with a homely environment and natural light), outpatient and community palliative care via **AlexNIC** nurses who offer symptom management, caregiver training, infusions, wound care and bereavement support.
- **Surgery & Anaesthesia Programme (SNAP)** | Delivers a comprehensive peri-operative journey, emphasising ambulatory and same-day surgery (hernia repairs, urological, ENT and eye procedures). Uses minimally invasive and robotic techniques for knee replacement and cervical spine surgery, reducing length of stay and enhancing recovery.
- **Psychological Medicine Programme** | Provides integrated mental health services across all age groups, including a **72-bed gazetted psychiatry ward**, generalist-led outpatient psychiatry, child & adolescent services and preventive community screening.
- **Rehabilitation Medicine Programme** | Offers centre-based rehabilitation and community partnerships. Specialises in spinal cord injury, stroke, paediatric neuro-rehabilitation, musculoskeletal & sports medicine, geriatric rehabilitation and cancer survivorship. Employs AI and tele-rehabilitation to personalise care and help patients reintegrate into the community.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Integrated General Hospital (IGH) model > Core programmes

text: ## Community outreach and patient engagement

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Community outreach and patient engagement

text:
### Community Care Coordination Unit (C3U)

The **C3U@AH** brings together clinicians, nurses and care managers to coordinate care across inpatient, outpatient, urgent care, nursing home and homecare settings. It assesses patient needs, guides families through healthcare options and supports caregivers. Operating Monday-Friday 9 am - 5:30 pm, C3U works closely with community partners to ensure seamless transitions.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Community outreach and patient engagement > Community Care Coordination Unit (C3U)

text:
### Care Beyond AH and telehealth

AH's **Care Beyond AH** initiative engages community partners and primary care networks to empower patients outside the hospital. **CareHub** telehealth allows patients to address healthcare needs via teleconsult, while **NUHS@Home** supports chronic disease management and some emergency care at home. The goal is to create a health-empowering community anchored by preventive care and early intervention.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Community outreach and patient engagement > Care Beyond AH and telehealth

text:
### Community Health Post (CHP)

In October 2024 AH opened its first **Community Health Post** at the Queenstown Multi-Service Centre. The CHP operates on Saturdays to serve working older adults and provides preventive care plans, chronic disease management, health coaching and basic geriatric assessments. By October 2024 it was the **14th CHP in Queenstown** and **64th in the western region**. The programme helps discharged patients manage chronic conditions at home, reducing readmissions.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Community outreach and patient engagement > Community Health Post (CHP)

text:
### ALEX H.E.A.L.

**ALEX H.E.A.L.** (Help, Engage, Assist Lives) is AH's official patient and family engagement programme launched in July 2024. Its aims are supported by three pillars: **Alex Advocates** (volunteers), **arts performances** and **community collaborations**. Volunteers serve as wayfinders, befrienders and health screening assistants, enriching patients' lives. Music and arts groups perform for patients, and community partners organise activities such as Iftar events and school visits.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Community outreach and patient engagement > ALEX H.E.A.L.

text: ## Research, innovation and technology

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Research, innovation and technology

text:
### Healthcare Redesign and Smart Ward

AH's **Healthcare Redesign Team** uses technology to transform care delivery. The **Smart Ward** functions as a living laboratory, featuring:

* **Switchable privacy glass**, **circadian lighting**, and **pod design** for infection control.
* **Modular walls** that expand bed capacity during surges.
* **AI-powered smart beds** with sensors to monitor patient posture and predict falls; **AI computer vision** that tracks patient movement; **smart glasses** enabling remote participation by off-site doctors; and a **3-D food scanner** that documents meal portions for nutritional analysis.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Research, innovation and technology > Healthcare Redesign and Smart Ward

text:
### Healthy Longevity Clinic and Centre for Healthy Longevity

Singapore is investing heavily in **longevity medicine**. In **September 2023**, AH opened the world's **first Healthy Longevity Medicine Clinic** at a public hospital. The clinic uses Singapore-specific ageing biomarkers and research from the **NUHS Centre for Healthy Longevity (CHL)** to delay biological ageing and enhance healthspan. CHL, launched in September 2022, focuses on geroscience and conducts clinical trials with support from a S$5 million gift from the Lien Foundation. The clinic offers diagnostic tests measuring biological age and interventions that may lower biological age, aligning with Singapore's Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Research, innovation and technology > Healthy Longevity Clinic and Centre for Healthy Longevity

text:
### Mind Art Experiential Lab (MAELab) and Mind Gym

The **D.S. Lee Foundation Mind Art Experiential Lab (MAELab)**, located at Alexandra Hospital, is an innovative space for exploring creative and integrative interventions through arts, mindfulness and research to promote mental wellness. It provides a flexible multipurpose venue for activities, workshops and exhibitions and hopes to fund initiatives demonstrating the benefits of creative arts in healthcare. Housed within MAELab, the **Mind Gym** offers mindfulness-based programmes-including lunchtime practice sessions, an eight-week structured course and half-day silent retreats-to cultivate mental fitness for patients, caregivers and the public.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Research, innovation and technology > Mind Art Experiential Lab (MAELab) and Mind Gym

text:
### Archaeology and heritage research

Before redevelopment works began, an archaeological study commissioned by the National Heritage Board uncovered charred Japanese wartime literature, British and Japanese helmets, water bottles and glass ampoules buried within the grounds. These artefacts provide tangible evidence of the hospital's wartime history and will be displayed in a heritage gallery when the redeveloped campus opens.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Research, innovation and technology > Archaeology and heritage research

text:
### Culinary innovation

In July 2025 AH launched a **Featured Chef Menu** in collaboration with Michelin-starred chef **Emmanuel Stroobant** of the restaurant Saint Pierre. The menu, served once a week at no additional cost, uses steaming and boiling techniques, reduced salt and no heavy sauces to create nutritious yet appetising dishes. Stroobant views the collaboration as a way to give back to the community and challenge stereotypes of bland hospital food. The menu has received praise from patients and demonstrates AH's commitment to patient experience.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Research, innovation and technology > Culinary innovation

text: ## Admissions, discharge and payment policies

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Admissions, discharge and payment policies

text:
### Admissions

Patients may be admitted internally (through the Urgent Care Centre) or externally (via referrals). AH staff provide information on appointment dates, financial counselling and estimated charges. Patients are advised to bring identity documents, work permits, insurance cards, toiletries and slippers but avoid valuables. The hospital offers several **ward classes**: **A1 (1-bed)**, **B1 (4-bed)**, **B2 (6-bed)** and **C (8-bed)**. Air-conditioned rooms, meal choices, personal phones or TVs and other amenities vary by ward type.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Admissions, discharge and payment policies > Admissions

text:
### Discharge procedures

Discharge typically takes place between **10 am and 11.30 am**. Nurses inform patients of their discharge timing, arrange medication supply and follow-up appointments, teach self-care and ensure that personal items are returned. Staying after noon may incur an additional day's fee.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Admissions, discharge and payment policies > Discharge procedures

text:
### Visiting hours and policies

Ward visiting hours are **10 am - 10 pm**, with a maximum of **two visitors** at the bedside. Children under 12 are not allowed in wards. Mask-wearing is mandatory in the Urgent Care Centre and inpatient wards but optional in outpatient clinics and day surgery. Critically ill patients may have up to **five visitors**. For patients with acute respiratory infections, visitor numbers are restricted to minimise infection risks.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Admissions, discharge and payment policies > Visiting hours and policies

text:
### Payment options

AH advises patients to pay their bills upon discharge. Payment methods include cash, major credit cards, NETS, cheques and digital platforms such as the NUHS App, HealthHub, AXS e-station or m-station, DBS internet banking/PayLah!, SAM, and PayNow. Refunds are processed after bill finalisation, and physical bills can be mailed upon request.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Admissions, discharge and payment policies > Payment options

text:
## Education, talent development and scholarships

AH offers **healthcare sponsorships and scholarships** to nurture future nurses, allied health professionals and pharmacists. Sponsored students join **Club Alex**, which provides fireside chats with senior management, networking sessions, tuition and career coaching. Eligibility criteria include being a Singapore citizen or permanent resident, being matriculated in relevant programmes, possessing good results and co-curricular records, and for mid-term sponsorships, having at least six months of course duration remaining. Applicants must submit a resume, sponsorship application form and academic transcripts via email. MOH Holdings also offers prestigious scholarships for nursing, pharmacy and allied health students to pursue studies locally or overseas.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Education, talent development and scholarships

text:
## Gardens, wellness and heritage experiences

AH's campus is known for its **lush gardens and medicinal plant collections**. The medicinal garden opened in 2005 and contains plants with healing properties. Nature trails and butterfly habitats offer tranquility for patients and visitors. The Therapeutic Horticulture Programme integrates gardening into rehabilitation. In addition, the campus will feature memory markers and heritage trails along the Rail Corridor as part of the redevelopment.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Gardens, wellness and heritage experiences

text:
### Mind Art Experiential Lab and creative wellbeing

Visitors can explore the **Mind Art Experiential Lab (MAELab)** at Block 29, Level 2. This space features rotating exhibitions on mental health themes and integrative arts interventions. Within MAELab, the **Mind Gym** offers mindfulness-based programmes to help participants cultivate mental fitness; activities include virtual lunchtime practice sessions and structured eight-week courses.

metadata.section: Comprehensive Overview of Alexandra Hospital (Singapore) > Gardens, wellness and heritage experiences > Mind Art Experiential Lab and creative wellbeing

text:
## Conclusion

Alexandra Hospital is a pioneering institution that combines rich heritage with innovative, integrated care models. As it redevelops into a 1 300-bed campus, AH continues to pilot novel programmes-from longevity medicine and smart wards to community health posts and therapeutic gardens-while remaining deeply rooted in the community. Its commitment to person-centred care, education and research ensures that the hospital not only honours its past but also shapes the future of healthcare in Singapore.

Q: When was Alexandra Hospital built and opened?
Q: What is the history of Alexandra Hospital?
Q: When was Alexandra Hospital handed over to the Ministry of Health?

A:
Selected Alexandra Hospital heritage milestones (from AH heritage page):
- 1938: British Military Hospital constructed on a 32-acre site.
- 1940: Hospital opens as a 356-bed facility serving as the main military hospital in the region.
- WWII period: expanded to 550 beds and reportedly stretched to ~900 patients at peak; about 200 staff and patients were killed during an attack by Japanese soldiers.
- 1971: official handover from the British to Singapore's Ministry of Health (MOH); renamed Alexandra Road General Hospital and reopened as a general civilian hospital.

- Designed as a community touchpoint offering easier access to healthcare within the community for working older adults.
- Provides essential health services and education on selected Saturdays.
- Focus areas include preventive care plan support, chronic disease management, and health education to increase health literacy.
- Supports basic health monitoring and lifestyle changes via discussion and trend review (e.g., BMI, blood pressure, glucose).
- A newsroom quote notes Queenstown precinct has about 120,000 residents and ~35% are working older adults.
